newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese bishops criticise parliamentary polls.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese bishops criticise parliamentary polls.

text.p: Lebanon's Maronite Catholic bishops have strongly criticised the country's parliamentary elections, saying the first three rounds of the five-stage polls showed that the democratic system was losing ground.

"The three stages of the polls in Mount Lebanon, north Lebanon and Beirut have shown that the democratic system in whose shadow we live is heading to retreat," the Council of Maronite Bishops said in a statement published by Beirut newspapers on Thursday.

Charges of electoral abuse marred the first three rounds of voting in which pro-government candidates won an overwhelming majority and opposition candidates, including Christian nationalists seeking a political comeback, were crushed.

Violations alleged by the opposition, newspapers and an independent monitoring group include bribery, intimidation, faulty voters' lists, vote-counting fraud, votes cast for dead or emigre voters and exclusion of opposition candidates' observers from polling stations during voting and vote-counting.

"In addition to the breaches that took place in the past, there are the heinous methods cited by newspapers which prompted a number of winning and losing candidates to complain of the state's bias to one party without the other," the bishops said.

"This is due to the election law which does not treat citizens equally...and this is why there was a boycott (of the polls), even though not a complete one, and indifference to them especially among Christians," the statement added.

The council headed by Cardinal Nasrallah Boutros Sfeir, seen as the last effective Christian voice in Lebanon, cautioned against what it said was an attempt to reduce opposition in parliament as this would have grave consequences for national unity.

"If the government responded to the demands of those who asked for a balanced elections law...we would not have witnessed these harsh criticisms which may lead to appeals against the validity of these polls," the bishops' statement added.

Three opposition candidates who lost in the first rounds have said they were preparing appeals to the Constitutional Council, a high court which could cancel the votes if it found that serious violations occurred.
South Lebanon votes on Sunday and the eastern Bekaa Valley the following Sunday.
